# aitmproxy MCP tool reference

<!-- GENERATED FILE — do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Regenerate: `node aitmproxy-plugin/scripts/gen-tool-reference.mjs` -->

This reference is generated by `aitmproxy-plugin/scripts/gen-tool-reference.mjs`
from the command listing the `aitm` binary prints on its usage error
(`target/debug/aitm --help`; `--help` is not a real flag, the CLI answers
`expected a command before flags` and lists every command with its parameters on
stderr). The `browser.confine` row and the `scan.*` section were added by hand
from the command schemas in source, because the binary the listing was last
captured from predates them; regenerate from a current build to refresh the rest.

Tool names are shown in dot form (`flow.list`), as the MCP server exposes them;
the one-shot `aitm` CLI accepts the same commands space-separated
(`aitm flow list`). The Parameters column uses the CLI spelling (`--id <flow-id>`,
`[--mode <string>]` optional); over MCP the same names are the keys of the tool's
JSON arguments, e.g. `{ "id": "<flow-id>" }`. Note that the one-shot CLI runs its own
in-process core and cannot steer a running proxy; drive a live proxy over MCP or
from the web UI, the TUI or the macOS app.

**67 tools across 16 namespaces.** When L4 is enabled in `config.yaml`
(`l4.enabled: true`) the `l4.*` family (interfaces, capture, craft, inject,
send/recv, in-path intercept, scope, agent gates) is registered as well; it needs
elevated privileges, is Linux-first, and is not listed here.

## `flow.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flow.list` | — | List the ids of every captured flow, oldest first. |
| `flow.get` | `--id <flow-id>` | Summarize one captured flow: kind, request line, status, state. |
| `flow.table` | — | Per-flow summaries for a flows table: method, URL, status, duration, state, and marks, oldest first. Read-only. |
| `flow.subscribe` | `[--filter <json-object>] [--since <flow-id>]` | Subscribe to live flow notifications on this connection. Returns a sub_id; matching flows then arrive as notifications/aitm/flow lines with no further request. Read-only. |
| `flow.unsubscribe` | `--sub_id <int>` | Cancel a flow subscription on this connection. Read-only. |
| `flow.detail` | `--id <flow-id> [--body <string>] [--offset <int>] [--length <int>]` | Full detail for one flow: headers, bodies, connection info, timing and edit state. `body` selects none\|inline\|range (default inline). |
| `flow.mark` | `--id <flow-id> --marks <json-array>` | Replace a flow's highlight mark set (e.g. colour names); an empty array clears it. |
| `flow.comment` | `--id <flow-id> --text <string>` | Set a flow's free-text comment; an empty string clears it. |
| `flow.replay` | `--id <flow-id>` | Reissue a captured HTTP request through the proxy client; returns the new flow's id. |
| `flow.intercept` | `[--enabled <true\|false>] [--rules <json-array>]` | Arm (default) or disarm interception. With no rules every request is parked (global arm); with rules only a request matching a rule at its phase is parked. A parked flow waits for flow.resume or flow.kill. |
| `flow.resume` | `--id <flow-id>` | Release an intercepted flow so its (possibly mutated) request is forwarded. |
| `flow.kill` | `--id <flow-id> [--mode <string>]` | Abort an intercepted flow. mode=reset (default) drops it so the client sees a reset/closed connection; mode=429 or mode=503 answers the client with that status and an empty body, with no upstream request. |
| `flow.clear` | — | Remove completed flows from the store (in-flight and intercepted flows are kept); returns {cleared, skipped_in_flight}. |
| `flow.mutate` | `--id <flow-id> --edits <json-object>` | Edit a captured HTTP flow in place. Edits apply to the request (method, path, headers, body); when the flow is parked at the response phase they apply to the response and `status` is valid. |
| `flow.export` | `[--ids <json-array>] [--format <string>] [--path <string>]` | Export selected flows (or the whole store) as `aitm` native JSON or HAR 1.2. Returns bytes, or writes to `path` when given. |
| `flow.import` | `[--path <string>] [--bytes <text>] [--format <string>]` | Import flows (by `path` or `bytes`) into the store, marked `imported`. Formats: `aitm`, `har`, or mitmproxy `.flows`. Passive: no upstream requests, never replays. |

## `proxy.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proxy.status` | — | The proxy's live state: `listening` (bool) + `address`, `intercept_armed`, `paused` (parked-flow count), `capturing`, and `flows` (visible count). |
| `proxy.pause` | — | Pause capture: new flows are hidden from list/status/count. Traffic still flows and each hidden flow stays in memory, reachable by id, until it ages out via normal eviction (use flow.clear to drop completed ones). While paused, continued traffic can evict older visible flows under the store's capacity bound, so resume or clear to reclaim history. Returns the capture state. |
| `proxy.resume` | — | Resume capture: new flows are shown again. Returns the capture state. |

## `scope.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scope.add` | `--host <string>` | Add a host, host:port, or *.wildcard to the active scope. Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless scope.allow_agent_widen is set. |
| `scope.remove` | `--host <string>` | Remove a scope entry (exact match). Narrowing scope is allowed from any frontend; returns true if an entry was removed. |
| `scope.list` | — | List the current scope entries. |

## `ws.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws.intercept` | `[--enabled <true\|false>] [--rules <json-array>]` | Arm (default) or disarm WebSocket frame interception and set the Phase::WsFrame rules that select which live frames are parked for ws.frame to edit/forward or drop. |
| `ws.frame` | `--id <flow-id> --index <int> --action <string> [--data <text>] [--opcode <string>]` | Act on a parked WebSocket frame: forward it (optionally editing its data/opcode first) or drop it so the peer never receives it. |
| `ws.send` | `--id <flow-id> --dir <string> --opcode <string> --data <text>` | Compose a new WebSocket frame and inject it onto a live conversation. Active egress: refused unless the flow's host is in scope. |

Refused from an agent frontend unless maps.allow_agent_authoring is set. |

| `map.remove` | `--id <string>` | Remove a Map rule by id. Refused from an agent frontend unless maps.allow_agent_authoring is set. |

## `ca.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ca.export` | `[--format <string>] [--out <string>]` | Export the aitmproxy root CA certificate (never its key) as PEM or DER, with its SHA-256 and SHA-1 fingerprints and the CA directory. Always available. This is for TLS clients you bring yourself; the embedded obscura browser already trusts the CA through --ca-cert and needs no export. |
| `ca.status` | — | Report the aitmproxy root CA: whether ca.crt exists, its fingerprints and path, and, per trust-store scope on this platform, whether a certificate with its fingerprint is installed and trusted. Read-only, always available, not audited. The embedded obscura browser does not use the OS store (it trusts the CA through --ca-cert), so these fields say nothing about it. |
| `ca.install` | `[--scope <string>] [--dry_run <true\|false>]` | Install the aitmproxy root CA into the OS trust store (macOS keychain via `security`, Linux ca-certificates anchors, Windows Root store via certutil); every TLS client that uses that store will then trust certificates this proxy mints. Idempotent; identifies the certificate by fingerprint; never reads the CA key. Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless ca.allow_agent_install is set in the aitmproxy config; dry_run is always allowed and lists the commands that would run. The embedded obscura browser does not use the OS store (it trusts the CA through --ca-cert) and is unaffected. |
| `ca.uninstall` | `[--scope <string>] [--dry_run <true\|false>]` | Remove the aitmproxy root CA from the OS trust store (macOS keychain via `security`, Linux ca-certificates anchors, Windows Root store via certutil); TLS clients that use that store stop trusting certificates this proxy mints. Idempotent; identifies the certificate by fingerprint; never reads the CA key. Refused from an agent frontend (MCP) unless ca.allow_agent_install is set in the aitmproxy config; dry_run is always allowed and lists the commands that would run. The embedded obscura browser does not use the OS store (it trusts the CA through --ca-cert) and is unaffected. |

## `agent.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.status` | `[--exclude_self <true\|false>]` | Report the current agent policy and recent agent activity. Read-only and readable by any role, but the activity count covers only the entries the caller may see: a caller that is not trusted control does not count entries made by trusted control (operator, CLI). |
| `agent.set` | `--policy <string>` | Set the agent policy (all \| auto \| ask \| readonly \| paused). The deliberate operator act that governs the agent — operator/CLI only; the agent cannot change its own policy. |
| `agent.activity` | `[--since <int>] [--limit <int>]` | Recent command-invocation audit entries (who ran what, with what redacted arguments, and the outcome), oldest first. A live view, not a complete record: a high-volume source can flush other sources' entries. `origin` is authoritative; `client_label` is an unauthenticated display string. A call with no `limit` can return at most 6144 entries at the default sizes, so pass `limit`. Read-only and readable by any role, but a caller that is not trusted control does not see entries made by trusted control (operator, CLI). |
| `agent.approve` | `--request_id <string> --allow <true\|false>` | Approve or deny a Sensitive agent command the server parked under the `ask` policy. Operator/CLI only; the agent cannot approve its own requests. |

## `script.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `script.validate` | `[--path <string>] [--source <string>]` | Compile a .rhai script without loading it; reports its name, API, hooks and the commands/options its load(reg) registers (a static scan; empty when the names are not literals), or the positioned compile error. Give exactly one of `path` (a file) or `source` (the script text, compiled in the sandbox with nothing written). |
| `script.reload` | `--name <string>` | Recompile a loaded script from its file and swap its hooks live; a failed recompile keeps the previous version. Commands and options it registered at load are unchanged until restart. |
| `script.findings` | `[--limit <int>]` | Findings scripts emitted with finding(...) this run (in-memory, not persisted): each as an object, oldest first, plus how many the bounded sink dropped. For the persistent store use findings.list/get/record. |
| `script.list` | — | List the loaded scripts in chain order: name, path, API, hooks, whether enabled, and the most recent hook error (null if none). |
| `script.enable` | `--name <string>` | Turn a loaded script's hooks back on live. Idempotent. Answers { name, enabled }. |
| `script.disable` | `--name <string>` | Turn a loaded script's hooks off live without unloading it; commands and options it registered stay (the registry is sealed). Idempotent. Answers { name, enabled }. |
| `script.save` | `--name <string> --source <string> [--enable <true\|false>]` | Write a script to <scripts_dir>/<name>.rhai after checking it compiles (a non-compiling source writes nothing). Its hooks go live immediately with no restart — for a brand-new name (appended to the running script host) as well as a save over a loaded script (swapped live). restart_required is true ONLY when the script registers commands or options, which the sealed registry cannot add until a restart; its hooks still run this session. Answers { name, path, api, hooks, registers, restart_required }. Needs rhai.scripts_dir. |

## `scan.*`

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scan.discover` | `--target <string> [--max_depth <int>] [--max_pages <int>]` | Discover reachable in-scope URLs under `target` (same-origin, scope-bound, budget-capped) and enumerate the injection points visible in captured requests. No injection or fuzzing is performed. `max_depth`/`max_pages` may lower the configured caps, never raise them. A navigation that lands off-origin or out of scope (a redirect) aborts the crawl with `stopped_reason = "left_scope"`. While the crawl runs the proxy's browser-egress posture is held confined, so the embedded browser cannot fetch an out-of-scope public host (sub-resource or redirect target); the hold is released when the command returns. Only one discovery runs at a time (crawls share one browser page); a second call while one is running is refused immediately — wait for it to finish. Needs the embedded browser for a real crawl; see `docs/scanner.md`. |
